title: Process String with Special Operations II
summary: Given a string s with lowercase English letters and special characters '*', '#', and '%', and an integer k, construct a new string result by applying the following rules from left to right: append a letter to result, remove the last character if '*', duplicate the result if '#', and reverse the result if '%'.
statement: Given a string s with lowercase English letters and special characters '*', '#', and '%', and an integer k, construct a new string result by applying the following rules from left to right: append a letter to result, remove the last character if '*', duplicate the result if '#', and reverse the result if '%'. Return the k^th character of result, or '.' if k is out of bounds.
constraints: The instruction string has up to 100,000 tokens.
The conceptual result length is at most 10^15 and k is zero-based.
Return a dot when k lies outside the final result.
hints: Only the result length is needed forward; the requested index can be mapped backward through operations.
Compute final length, reject an out-of-range k, then invert each token in reverse.
Undo doubling by folding k into the first half, undo reversal by mirroring, and identify the appended letter when its position is reached.
Each inverse mapping preserves the character occupying k without constructing the exponentially large result.
editorial: Each inverse mapping preserves the character occupying k without constructing the exponentially large result.

tests.explanation: The final string is ba, whose index one is a.
The final string dcddcd has d at index three.
